mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent risk aversion and reduced liquidity in the equity market.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a concurrent decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < INDPRO) signals a weakening labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < INDPRO by > 10% in the same month
failure_condition: In >70% of similar trigger events, the 20-day SPX forward return is non-negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not directly observable in the catalog but proxy via HOUST for units sold) exceed expectations by at least 5% for two consecutive months, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days tend to be positive as market anticipates sustained consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > baseline (last month) * 1.05 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 such triggers, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO > 110) for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as it signals robust manufacturing capacity and upward supply-side momentum.
failure_condition: In >60% of such supply expansions, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as markets anticipate rate cuts and liquidity injection by the Fed.
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggers, the 5-day forward return is not positive (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising labor participation (PAYEMS > previous month for two months) combined with a declining consumer price index (CPIAUCSL < previous month for two months) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days due to inflation-employment tradeoff concerns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month for two months AND CPIAUCSL < previous month for two months
failure_condition: In >80% of such dual triggers, the 60-day forward return is non-negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month followed by a sustained decline over the next month is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as markets anticipate a resumption of rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous month_value - 0.005 for month 1 AND CPIAUCSL < previous month_value for month 2
failure_condition: Across 10 such CPI drops, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows by more than 8% in a single month, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days is expected to be positive as the market anticipates robust economic momentum and potential rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous_month_value * 1.08 in a single month
failure_condition: In >70% of such monthly spikes, the 60-day forward return is not positive (p < 0.05).
